title: Texas Property Code, Chapter 116, Uniform Principal and Income Act
publication_date_or_edition: Official statutory text reviewed 2026-09-24; Texas Property Code, Chapter 116
accounting_bases: Texas fiduciary principal and income; distinct from federal DNI and financial reporting
source_classification: State statute; selected Texas fiduciary accounting authority
inspected_summary: Governing instrument and statutory defaults classify receipts/disbursements between principal and income; provides bounded adjustment power, death-time receipt allocations, termination and beneficiary records, security-income rules, and category-specific expense allocations.
locators: Tex. Prop. Code §§116.004-.005, .051-.052, .101-.102, .151-.163, .201-.202; selected sections on official HTML

evidence.observed: Instrument controls before defaults; unresolved receipts generally principal; adjustment power and expense split rules are limited; death-date income allocations and beneficiary records are separately specified.

access_limits: Selected Texas example only. Instrument, trust situs, statutory applicability, later amendments, and entity facts must be verified; no national rule inferred.
effective_dates_and_supersession: Official chapter text accessed 2026-09-24. Chapter and cited sections have differing enactment/amendment histories; verify section-specific effective law for the trust and transaction.

title: 26 CFR §1.643(b)-1, Definition of income
publisher: Internal Revenue Service, Treasury (official CFR at GovInfo)
accounting_bases: Federal fiduciary income tax; applicable instrument and local law supply trust-accounting income, subject to federal guardrails
inspected_summary: Defines Subchapter J trust/estate income by instrument and local law, subject to traditional-principles limits. Reasonable total-return apportionment and authorized local-law adjustments can be respected; unauthorized changes can have separate federal consequences.

title: 26 CFR §§1.643(a)-1 and 1.643(a)-3, Distribution deduction and capital gains/losses in DNI
publisher: Internal Revenue Service, Treasury (official CFR at GovInfo)
accounting_bases: Federal fiduciary income tax; DNI computation and beneficiary distribution character
inspected_summary: Distribution deductions are excluded when computing DNI. Capital gains ordinarily fall outside DNI; the regulation defines specific income-allocation, consistently-recorded distribution, actual-distribution/distribution-measurement, and charitable-deduction routes for inclusion. It also sets trust-level capital-loss netting rules.

evidence.observed: Gain inclusion routes in paragraph (b) carry the common governing-instrument/local-law or authorized reasonable-and-impartial-discretion condition; paragraph (c) separately includes gains supporting a §642(c) deduction; losses generally net at trust level.

access_limits: Selected mechanics only. Does not determine treatment without instrument, local law, fiduciary authority, return-year rules, and actual records.
effective_dates_and_supersession: Text verified in 2025 annual CFR; no later amendment review or 2026 return-year determination.

title: 26 CFR §1.671-4, Grantor trust reporting methods and death transition
publisher: Internal Revenue Service, Treasury (official CFR at GovInfo)
accounting_bases: Federal fiduciary information and income-tax reporting
inspected_summary: Owner-attributable items generally appear on an attached statement rather than as trust Form 1041 amounts; optional wholly grantor-owned reporting methods have conditions. When death ends ownership treatment, the affected portion may no longer report under this section; a continuing trust wholly owned by the decedent must obtain a new TIN.

evidence.observed: The default owner-item statement rule and conditional alternative methods are specified; death cessation changes reporting and requires a new TIN for a continuing wholly grantor-owned trust.

title: Revenue Ruling 2004-64, Tax reimbursement clause
accounting_bases: Federal grantor-trust income, gift-tax, and estate-tax treatment; not a general ledger standard
source_classification: Published IRS revenue ruling; federal interpretive authority on stated facts
inspected_summary: Grantor's payment of tax on grantor-attributed trust income discharges the grantor's own §671 liability and is not a gift to trust beneficiaries. Mandatory reimbursement can cause estate inclusion; discretionary authority alone does not, whether or not exercised, assuming no understanding. Other facts can change the result. IRS prospective application protects pre-Oct. 4, 2004 trusts from adverse application of the Situation 2 holding.
locators: Rev. Rul. 2004-64, Issues/Facts, Situations 1-3, analysis and Holdings; web lines 451-496

evidence.method: Direct IRS Internal Revenue Bulletin read
evidence.locator: Rev. Rul. 2004-64, especially Holdings and Prospective Application; lines 487-496
evidence.observed: Discretion not alone determinative whether or not exercised; pre-existing arrangement, replacement power, or creditor exposure may matter; IRS states the prospective application limit for pre-Oct. 4, 2004 trusts.

access_limits: Specific grantor/trust and reimbursement facts; not a universal estate inclusion or bookkeeping rule.
effective_dates_and_supersession: Published 2004 ruling. Its prospective-application paragraph says IRS will not apply the Situation 2 estate-tax holding adversely to estates of grantors for trusts created before Oct. 4, 2004. Later authority/facts must be checked.
rights: No source-specific reuse grant established. Link and original metadata/summary only; full text not stored.

title: 26 CFR §1.1014-1, Basis of property acquired from a decedent
publisher: Internal Revenue Service, Treasury (official CFR at GovInfo)
accounting_bases: Federal income-tax basis; related federal estate-tax valuation reference
inspected_summary: Provides the general date-of-death fair-market-value basis rule for qualifying property, alternate valuation date where elected under §2032, and limitations. §1014(c) excludes IRD rights from this basis rule. §1.1014-1 points to the separately sourced §1.1014-10 for consistent-basis rules.

evidence.observed: General basis equals estate-tax value at death or an elected alternate valuation date, for qualifying property and subject to limitations; §1.1014-1 directs readers to consistent-basis rules in §1.1014-10.

access_limits: General rule only; exceptions, asset-specific basis, gross-estate inclusion, community property, and valuation require separate review.
effective_dates_and_supersession: Verified in the 2025 annual CFR. The separately sourced §1.1014-10 contains the applicability date for its defined consistent-basis property; no broader conclusion on later amendments.

title: 26 CFR §1.1014-10, Consistent basis with federal estate-tax value
publisher: Internal Revenue Service, Treasury (official CFR at GovInfo)
accounting_bases: Federal income-tax basis consistency tied to federal estate-tax value
inspected_summary: For specified consistent-basis property, initial tax basis cannot exceed final federal estate-tax value or, while final value is unresolved, the reported estate-tax value. The requirement continues while basis remains related to that value, subject to the regulation’s scope and exceptions.
locators: 26 CFR §1.1014-10(a)(1)-(3), (b), (c), and (f); printed pp. 67-73; applicability date at printed p. 73

evidence.observed: Covered initial basis is limited to the final or reported federal estate-tax value; regulation defines included/excluded property, ongoing duration, and applicability to covered property when the decedent’s federal estate-tax return is filed after Sept. 17, 2024.

access_limits: Selected scope/limit and applicability mechanics only; the regulation has detailed property categories, exceptions, reporting/election facts, and examples that must be reviewed for an actual asset.
effective_dates_and_supersession: Under §1.1014-10(f), applies to property described in paragraph (c)(1) acquired from or by reason of a decedent if the decedent’s federal estate-tax return is filed after Sept. 17, 2024; T.D. 9991, 89 FR 76376 (Sept. 17, 2024).
